title: B2 · L8 — Reported speech (advanced)
description: Verbos de reporte avanzados: accuse, deny, suggest, warn, insist. Cada uno tiene su propia estructura sintáctica.

questions.prompt: Situación: cuentas un pequeño incidente en la oficina.
questions.question: Complete: 'She accused me ___ stealing her pen.'
options: for
of
to
about
questions.explanation: 'Accuse someone OF + gerundio' es una colocación fija. La preposición 'of' es obligatoria y no negociable. Error típico de hispanohablante: usar 'for' por calco de otras estructuras ('blame someone FOR'), pero cada verbo tiene su preposición. Memoriza: accuse OF, blame FOR, apologise FOR, congratulate ON.
examples: He accused her of lying about her whereabouts. → drama de oficina
The prosecution accused him of tax evasion over a five-year period.

questions.prompt: Reportas lo que un sospechoso dijo en un interrogatorio.
questions.question: Report: '"I didn't take the money," he said.'
options: He denied to take the money.
He denied taking the money.
He denied that took the money.
He denied he take the money.
questions.explanation: 'Deny' se construye con gerundio ('deny + -ing') o con 'that + oración completa'. NUNCA 'deny + to + infinitivo' — es error muy frecuente en hispanohablantes por calco de 'negar hacer'. Truco: memoriza que 'deny' pertenece al grupo de verbos que rechazan el 'to' + infinitivo (junto con admit, suggest, avoid, consider).
examples: She denied cheating in the game — the ref reviewed the tape anyway.
He denied having any prior knowledge of the plan. → registro legal formal

questions.statement: 'He suggested to go out for dinner' es correcto.
questions.explanation: FALSO — es uno de los errores más persistentes de hispanohablante. 'Suggest' NUNCA lleva 'to + infinitivo'. Las tres formas correctas son: (1) suggest + -ing, (2) suggest + that + subject + should + verb, (3) suggest + that + subject + verb (subjuntivo). El calco viene de 'sugerir hacer', pero en inglés no funciona así.
examples: Correct: He suggested going out for dinner. → informal, cotidiano
Correct: She suggested that we should postpone the meeting. → formal escrito

questions.text: The teacher warned us not to talk during the exam or we would be disqualified.
questions.explanation: 'Warn someone NOT TO + verbo' + consecuencia con 'or'. Connected speech: 'warned us' se fusiona 'wɔːnd-ʌs', y 'not to talk' se pronuncia rápido con la /t/ de 'not' glotalizada antes de 'to' → 'no(t)-tə'. Es la estructura clásica de advertencias serias con amenaza implícita.
examples: She warned him not to touch the wires or he'd get an electric shock. → aviso doméstico
The guide warned us not to leave the marked path — bears in the area.

questions.prompt: Un amigo generoso insistió en pagar la cena.
questions.question: Complete: 'He insisted ___ paying for everyone's meal.'
options: in
on
at
for
questions.explanation: 'Insist ON + gerundio' es colocación fija. Alternativa: 'insist that + subject + should/verb' en registro más formal. Nota que en español decimos 'insistir en' — la traducción literal aquí SÍ funciona, pero no confíes en el instinto: comprueba siempre porque 'insist for' o 'insist about' son errores frecuentes.
examples: She insisted on doing the dishes even though we'd offered to hire help. → gesto amable
They insisted on paying the entire bill. Very generous of them.

questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Los tres verbos comparten la construcción con gerundio (-ing form) o con 'that + clause', pero NUNCA con 'to + infinitive'. Pertenecen al grupo de 'verbos mentales/comunicativos' que rechazan el infinitivo con 'to'. Truco mnemotécnico: A-D-S (Admit-Deny-Suggest) = 'always -ing, no to'.
examples: He finally admitted stealing the money after weeks of denials.
She suggested waiting a bit longer before making a decision.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada verbo reportado con su patrón sintáctico correcto:

pairs.right: having any involvement in the crime.
not to go out after dark.

questions.explanation: Cada verbo tiene su propia arquitectura: deny + gerundio, accuse of + gerundio, warn (not) to + infinitivo, insist ON + gerundio, apologise FOR + gerundio. Como no hay lógica unificada, la única estrategia es memorizarlos como bloques. Estos cinco son los más frecuentes en exámenes B2 First.
examples: He apologised for being rude in the meeting — genuine and unprompted.
She admitted forgetting the appointment — happens to the best of us.

questions.prompt: Reportas lo que dijo tu profesora en tutoría.
questions.question: Report: '"You should study harder," the teacher said.'
options: The teacher recommended me to study harder.
The teacher recommended studying harder.
The teacher recommended I should study harder.
The teacher recommended studying harder OR that I (should) study harder.
questions.explanation: 'Recommend' funciona exactamente como 'suggest': acepta (1) recommend + -ing o (2) recommend + that + subject + (should) + verb. NUNCA 'recommend someone to do' — es error frecuente por calco del español 'recomendarle a alguien'. En inglés hay que reformular con 'that clause' si mencionas la persona.
examples: She recommended taking the train — cheaper and more scenic than flying.
The doctor recommended that I rest for at least a week before returning to work.

questions.target: The manager congratulated us on completing the project ahead of schedule.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate + someone + ON + gerundio' es la fórmula profesional estándar (nunca 'for' — error común). Prosodia formal, con énfasis en 'ahead of schedule'. Nativos añaden matices: 'as well as under budget', 'which is quite an achievement' para reforzar el cumplido.
examples: He congratulated her on her promotion to head of marketing. → email corporativo
They congratulated me on passing the Cambridge C1 exam — meant a lot.

questions.prompt: Identifica el verbo que rompe el patrón.
questions.question: Which verb takes 'someone + to + infinitive'?
options: deny
suggest
advise
admit
questions.explanation: 'Advise' es especial: acepta 'someone + to + infinitivo' ('I advised him to leave') y también 'advise + -ing' sin objeto ('I advise leaving early'). Es el único del grupo con esa flexibilidad. Los otros tres (deny, suggest, admit) sólo aceptan gerundio o 'that clause', nunca objeto + infinitivo.
examples: The doctor advised me to rest for a week. → uso con objeto
I'd advise leaving before rush hour — traffic gets brutal. → uso sin objeto

questions.statement: 'He threatened to sue the company' es una estructura de reporte correcta.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Threaten + to + infinitivo' expresa una amenaza directa dirigida al oyente/tercero. Alternativa: 'threaten + that + clause' para más formalidad. Nota que 'threaten' es uno de los pocos verbos de reporte que SÍ admite 'to + infinitivo' — pertenece al grupo de intenciones futuras (promise, offer, refuse, agree, threaten).
examples: He threatened to call the police if we didn't turn the music down. → conflicto vecinal
She threatened to resign if working conditions didn't improve. → tensión laboral

questions.text: She apologised for missing the meeting and offered to reschedule it for Friday.
questions.explanation: Dos verbos reportados en una frase: 'apologise FOR + gerundio' y 'offer + TO + infinitivo'. Prosodia cortés y profesional. Connected speech: 'apologised for' fluye como 'əpɒlədʒaɪzd-fə', y 'offered to' se enlaza con schwa. Nota los dos patrones distintos en una sola oración — clave del registro profesional.
examples: He apologised for being late and offered to buy the whole team coffee. → gesto reparador
She apologised for the technical error and promised to fix it by end of day.

questions.prompt: Reportas la respuesta entusiasta de un amigo a tu invitación.
questions.question: Report: '"I'll definitely come to the party," he said.'
options: He promised to come to the party.
He offered coming to the party.
He denied to come to the party.
He suggested to come to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Promise + to + infinitivo' captura la firmeza que aporta 'definitely'. La elección del verbo de reporte transmite el matiz de la intención original: 'promise' (firmeza), 'offer' (ofrecimiento voluntario), 'agree' (aceptación tras propuesta ajena), 'threaten' (amenaza). El verbo importa más que el mensaje literal.
examples: He promised to help me move next weekend. → compromiso amistoso
She promised to be there on time — and she actually was, for once.

questions.target: He admitted forgetting my birthday but insisted on making it up to me with a special dinner.
questions.explanation: Combinación clásica de dos verbos avanzados: 'admit + gerundio' + 'insist ON + gerundio'. Estructura muy natural para narrar mini-conflictos y reconciliaciones. 'Make it up to someone' es phrasal idiomático B2 (compensar a alguien). Prosodia: pausa suave tras 'birthday' y énfasis emotivo en 'special dinner'.
examples: She admitted breaking the vase but offered to replace it with something nicer.
He denied lying and insisted on his innocence — the whole thing was awkward.

questions.prompt: Detecta el error en el uso de 'remind'.
questions.question: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
options: She reminded me to lock the door.
She reminded me locking the door.
She reminded me that I had to lock the door.
She reminded me about locking the door.
questions.explanation: 'Remind' acepta tres estructuras: (1) remind + someone + TO + infinitivo (recordar hacer), (2) remind + someone + that + clause, (3) remind + someone + ABOUT + sustantivo/gerundio (recordar algo). NUNCA 'remind + someone + gerundio' directamente. La opción B mezcla mal las dos últimas.
examples: Remind me to call Mum tomorrow — I keep forgetting. → petición cotidiana
He reminded her about paying the rent by the 5th to avoid the late fee.
